cards.title: Exact scope
items: This is the non-preview, ordinary collection-effect branch of API execute, also used by API-backed CLI commands.

Read-only and dry-run requests skip these mutation steps. Staging and non-collection filesystem writes use file-only history; unresolved filesystem effects reserve exclusive access before classification.
Creation has no existing databases to back up. Sync and undo manage their own history paths. Those specialized flows are outside this drawing.

cards.title: Recovery semantics
items: Desktop running or an unknown check result stops execution before backups or history writes. Linux reports the supported negative process result without scanning.
The backup path uses SQLite online backup to include committed WAL pages and publishes only after all copies succeed.
History locks the library, removes only unreferenced storage, captures before state, runs the mutation, then captures actual after state even after cancellation or failure.
If after capture fails, the pending entry and originals remain for recovery. Failed mutations retain undo records; failures confined to declared acquisition workspaces discard their history entry.

cards.title: Undo is a separate operation
items: A completed history entry records changed entities and reversible file moves. Database-only changes do not back up unrelated audio or artwork.
Undo checks for conflicting later edits and refuses by default. An explicit force override permits conflict recovery; dry-run previews remain read-only.

cards.title: Bulk metadata — after the pinned revision
items: track.batch.update accepts 1–500 selectors and common scalar metadata. The ordinary collection-write path supplies Desktop protection, one safety snapshot, and one history record.

EditMetadataBatch resolves every selector before writing, deduplicates aliases in first-seen order, and saves all fields in one transaction. Missing selectors or failed writes leave the collection unchanged. The result contains track_ids without rereading committed entities.
The CLI exposes the same edit as track batch update. One undo restores the entire edit. This behavior was committed in 07441d1 after the source revision pinned above.

cards.title: M3U import — committed extension
items: playlist.import and playlist import create a new playlist from existing collection tracks only. A read-only preview resolves server-local M3U/M3U8 paths, preserves first-seen track order, reports duplicate and unresolved entries, and requires an explicit reviewed skip policy. No acquisition, append, or replacement occurs.

Apply checks the exact review before Desktop checks, safety backups, or history creation. The token binds source bytes, normalized options, library UUID and canonical root, resolved track identities, and origins. Stale or blocked reviews fail without mutation artifacts.

Apply rebuilds and checks the plan inside one transaction, then creates the playlist and every ordered membership together. Cancellation or an insertion failure rolls back the entire playlist. The ordinary collection-write path supplies Desktop protection, the configured safety backup, and one history entry; one undo reverses the import.

Evidence: cbac846503e303552ed223020d47a37f3c3783a9, internal/api/playlist_import.go:12–38; internal/api/operations.go:175–234; internal/playlist/import.go:73–108,164–282. This extension is separate from the historical revision pinned above. Uncommitted working-tree changes are outside this review.

cards.title: M3U export — read source, write destination
items: playlist.export and playlist export review direct playlist memberships in saved nextEntityId order, including every origin identity. Malformed links fail; unavailable media blocks export unless the exact review explicitly includes skipping it. UTF-8, Windows-1252, or Latin-1 output and absolute or destination-relative paths are validated before creating a file; M3U8 requires UTF-8.

Preview and apply hold the collection read barrier. Each review reads the playlist title, memberships, and library UUID in one read-only transaction. Apply rebuilds the review and matches its token before publication; the token binds source identities, normalized options, availability, and serialized output. The read transaction ends before the destination is created, while API scheduling retains the source read barrier.

Non-preview apply also takes the shared write gate to serialize its output-file write. Its catalog effect remains read: it does not modify the source collection and skips Desktop checks, safety backups, history, and undo. This specialized path is outside the ordinary collection-write drawing above.

Publication opens the destination parent with os.OpenRoot and exclusively creates a new file with O_CREATE|O_EXCL. Existing files, directories, and symlinks are refused; no overwrite, append, or audio copy occurs. The file can be visible while writing. Write, sync, close, or cancellation failures attempt cleanup only while the path still identifies the created file; cleanup is best-effort and preserves external replacements.

Evidence: 9c9a37eeea33b447fbb33217cac2cdbbfc6b8646, internal/api/playlist_export.go:14–30; internal/api/scheduling.go:9–41; internal/api/operations.go:175–241; internal/playlist/export.go:81–173; internal/playlist/export_order.go:23–80; internal/playlist/export_file.go:13–70. Historical evidence pins remain unchanged. Uncommitted working-tree changes are outside this review.

cards.title: Track analysis and grid saves — after the pinned revision
items: track.analyze uses the ordinary collection-write path for its one safety snapshot and history record, then analyzes up to four tracks concurrently and writes each in its own transaction. Before every write it rechecks Engine DJ Desktop, so a long batch stops before its next write when Desktop starts; tracks already written stay covered by the same undo record.

Analysis keeps a saved grid's sample rate, writes analyzed grids to both stored vectors, respects isBeatGridLocked, and never sets isAnalyzed. Per-track no_beat, no_key and audio failures are result outcomes, not job failures. track.add and staging.import with analyze:true run the same analysis after their imports.

track.grid.update refuses grids locked in Engine DJ, requires the draft to reach the saved sample-length limit, and replaces only the adjusted grid with the matching BPM; POST tracks/{id}/beatgrid/edits computes drafts read-only and never enters this path. Failed or stopped runs still report the tracks and imports they wrote. Committed in 050ada5, b333e89 and 2434750 after the source revision pinned above.

cards.title: Custom tags — committed addition: validation before mutation artifacts
items: Custom-tag category/value edits, exact track assignment replacements, deletions and orphan reconciliation share the ordinary collection-write path. Bound preflight checks run before Desktop checks, automatic backups and history creation: invalid names, duplicate names, missing targets, stale revisions and mismatched review tokens fail there.

Companion writes enforce foreign keys on the same physical connection used for the transaction, re-read the stored revision, and recheck the operation inside that transaction. Preview deletion and reconciliation remain read-only. An empty assignment list explicitly clears values; omission is rejected.

Reviewed committed evidence 56cee6e56c5001e0d68795442cc3b7a72856df39: internal/api/tags.go:39–120; internal/api/operations.go:177–244; internal/tags/validation.go:9–82; internal/tags/edit.go:12–73. The historical source pins remain unchanged. Historical workflow nodes and links retain their original evidence.

cards.title: Custom tags — committed addition: explicit orphan consent
items: External Engine removals leave stored assignments intact. List counts include only available native origins and report unavailable origins separately, without changing the stored revision. tag.reconcile previews exactly those missing-origin assignments and requires its reviewed token and revision on apply.

Deletion impact separates currently affected Engine origins from all removed assignments, including unavailable ones. Delete tokens bind the live affected-origin set as well as stored revision. Reconciliation tokens bind exact missing assignments; both are rechecked during apply.

Ordinary collection history prunes only origins present before and removed by that operation, preserving pre-existing external orphans. Duplicate merging unions assignments onto the survivor. Browsing, renaming and unrelated edits do not silently reconcile missing origins.

Reviewed committed evidence 56cee6e56c5001e0d68795442cc3b7a72856df39: internal/tags/store.go:192–222; internal/tags/delete.go:10–88; internal/tags/reconcile.go:22–89; internal/tags/lifecycle.go:19–41,69–91; internal/duplicate/merge.go:96–106. The historical source pins remain unchanged.

cards.title: Custom tags — committed addition: companion recovery boundary
items: Collection history captures enrolled Engine and companion databases with native database snapshots. Backups record explicit companion presence; restore validates that presence and database integrity before live writes. Undo preserves conflict checks and can reverse companion creation or removal.

A durable pending history entry precedes execution. Sync validates both companion revisions before committing Engine changes, then publishes companion and identity/sync state separately. If a later publication fails, retained pending history requires explicit inspected recovery rather than a blind retry.

Sync is a specialized path, outside the ordinary workflow above. Its name/reference conflict checks and tag_assignments_stale refusal protect the planned taxonomy and assignments; external orphan cleanup requires a separate reviewed reconciliation.

Reviewed committed evidence 56cee6e56c5001e0d68795442cc3b7a72856df39: internal/history/files.go:57–104; internal/history/history.go:161–264; internal/history/undo.go:53–109; internal/backup/companion.go:26–117; internal/backup/restore.go:40–83; internal/transfer/tags.go:15–43,157–190; internal/transfer/apply.go:133–171. The historical source pins remain unchanged.

cards.title: Batch custom tags — exact consent and atomic companion write
items: Batch inspection and dry-run review are read-only. The plan preserves first-seen resolved track order, rejects duplicate or overlapping value actions, and reports changed tracks separately from added and removed native-origin assignments. Multiple library rows sharing one native origin change that assignment only once.

The checked API preflight rejects stale revision or token, missing values and zero-change apply before Desktop checks, safety backup or history creation. A zero-change preview remains valid; an apply reports tag_no_changes rather than creating a misleading history entry.

Apply re-resolves native identities, checks the token and revision again inside the companion transaction, then deletes and inserts all assignments atomically. An error or cancellation rolls back that transaction. The ordinary collection operation supplies the existing snapshot and one undo entry; this does not claim atomic publication across Engine, companion and history files.

Reviewed committed evidence 8e33df9d106215b5fd9723c82800867c72b670c6: internal/api/tags.go:126–138; internal/tags/batch.go:60–79,129–192,195–263; internal/api/tags_batch_test.go:17–155. Historical workflow nodes, links and evidence pins remain unchanged.

cards.title: Metadata find/replace — preflight, one transaction, one Undo
items: Dry-run find/replace is a collection read. Apply uses checked preflight before fresh Desktop protection, safety snapshots and history: the exact token binds library identity, canonical root, selected identities, options and current metadata. Stale review, invalid titles, no changes or resource-budget failures never enroll mutation artifacts.

Inside the ordinary protected write, ApplyFindReplace rebuilds the review in the same transaction that saves every changed field. It checks the token again, preserves unselected and null values, and returns affected IDs only after commit. Cancellation or any failed write rolls back the batch; the surrounding ordinary collection operation provides one snapshot and one undo record.

The transform checks SQL byte lengths before hydrating evidence, caps native match-index storage, and bounds each native capture expansion before allocation. These limits also apply during transactional revalidation, rather than trusting an earlier preview. Native regex matching is not individually interruptible; bounded inputs and context checkpoints limit the work between cancellation observations.

Reviewed committed evidence 18a4587f84bc9cfe799395ed28f03d2c0f77ff43: internal/api/find_replace.go:12–37; internal/track/find_replace.go:126–142,201–339; internal/track/bounded_replace.go:49–103; internal/api/find_replace_test.go:16–138. Historical workflow nodes, links and evidence pins remain unchanged.

cards.title: Metadata capitalization — Unicode recipes and exact review
items: track.batch.capitalize and track batch capitalize apply upper, lower or title casing to eight selected collection text fields. Existing golang.org/x/text cases and language APIs own Unicode and BCP 47 semantics; an empty language uses language.Und rather than the host locale. Audio and embedded tags remain unchanged.

Read-only preview and checked apply share the metadata transformation owner with find/replace. Exact consent binds canonical library root, UUID, resolved identities, native origins, options and current metadata. Checked preflight runs before Desktop protection, snapshot and history; application rechecks the token inside one transaction and returns affected IDs after commit without rereading entities.

SQL byte-length checks precede hydration. Source evidence and outputs are bounded to 1 MiB per field and 16 MiB per batch. Whole-field casing supplies EOF for contextual word endings, resets before bounded expansion retries, and observes cancellation between attempts. Invalid recipes, languages, UTF-8 and empty resulting titles cannot authorize a write.

Reviewed committed evidence 195709a8a69741190a17c9f1732c739bfd8062f1: internal/track/capitalization.go:25–130; internal/track/metadata_transform.go:136–288; internal/api/capitalization.go:12–44. Historical graph and evidence pins remain unchanged; the ordinary collection writer retains Desktop, snapshot and single-Undo ownership. No separate actor or persistence store is introduced.
